newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down on long liquidation ahead of US data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down on long liquidation ahead of US data.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond futures ended slightly lower on Friday, as it was pushed down by a flurry of position adjustment sales which appeared toward the close.
"Dealers were probably reluctant to hold long positions ahead of the release of U.S. jobs data," a trust bank trader said.
U.S. February non-farm payroll data is due at 1330 GMT.
In a Reuters poll, economists estimated, on average, that payrolls expanded by 230,000 jobs in February after growing by 271,000 jobs in January.
The June ended at 125.31, down slightly from the previous day's 125.35.
Turnover was 62,201 contracts.
Investors were mostly inactive, seeing little reason to move before the release of the U.S. payroll data, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Investors will probably decide on investment strategies for the next fiscal year after taking a look at the U.S. jobs data, the trader said.
Traders said, however, that some selling of cash JGBs were seen on the upperside.
City banks were apparently selling the 193rd cash JGB, the trust bank trader said.
"Profit-taking sales were seen when JGBs surged in the early morning," the trader said.
Speculation that hedge funds may buy back JGB futures boosted JGBs in the morning, a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.

A rumour that an agricultural financial institution was planning to take delivery of cash JGBs from the March futures contract also contributed to the strong short-covering pressure, the trust bank trader said.
Traders with short positions in the March, who lacked deliverable cash JGB holdings, preferred to buy back the March rather than be forced to make delivery, the trader said.

Speculation that Tokyo share prices would fall in the morning due to Nomura Securities Co Ltd's announcement on Thursday that it was highly likely that two of its directors had been involved in illegal deals also provided momentum, the trust bank trader added.
But when an initial fall was less sharp than expected, JGBs gradually lost steam, he said.
In the Tokyo stock market, the key Nikkei 225 average ended at 18,198.74, up 157.41 points from Thursday's close.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is scheduled to announce its March long-term prime rate on Monday afternoon.
Judging from current market conditions, the rate is likely to be left steady at 2.5 percent, traders said.
The IBJ's February five-year bank debentures with a coupon rate of 1.6 percent were traded at 1.63 percent on Friday.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.350 percent as of 0713 GMT, down from Thursday's close of 2.360 percent.
